note.note:
Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes): Acute left-sided severe headache since waking this morning (~05:30). History of anxiety for ~2 years. No known diagnosis of hypertension or diabetes; patient reports never having BP checked. Recent increased work-related stress and several months of late nights (sleep disturbance). Possible dehydration risk discussed.  
- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes): Mother with history of anxiety; patient reports no family history of diagnosed migraines or major physical illnesses.  
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines: Sertraline — dose/route/frequency not documented. Paracetamol taken this morning — dose/route/frequency not documented. Ibuprofen recommended by clinician for acute headache (prescription/advice) — dose/route/frequency not documented. No known drug allergies.  
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus): Not recorded.  
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks: Not recorded.  
- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use: Runs ~3 times per week. Diet described as "OK" / "not unhealthy." Non-smoker. Recent pattern of late nights and increased workload for ~2 months. Alcohol and other substance use not recorded.  
- Hearing and vision concerns: Mild photophobia / light sensitivity causing eye soreness. No other hearing or vision concerns documented.  
- Mood, mental health, and risk assessment (depression, anxiety, self-harm): Anxiety history for ~2 years; currently taking sertraline. Current mood: not markedly low or angry, intermittent frustration related to work. Denies suicidal or self-harm thoughts.  
- Social context: family support, caregiving, housing, financial stressors: Lives with partner. Reports significant work backlog and stress. Has a pet cat. No other social determinants or financial/housing concerns recorded.

Examination

- Vital signs: BP, pulse rate and rhythm: Not recorded.  
- Anthropometry: height, weight, BMI, waist circumference if indicated: Not recorded.  
- Oral health: gums, teeth, dentures if relevant: Not recorded.  
- Ear exam including otoscopy: Not recorded.  
- Eye exam: visual acuity, pupil response, fundus if indicated: Not recorded (only symptom of mild light sensitivity reported).  
- Urinalysis: dipstick for protein, glucose, ketones, blood: Not recorded.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Blood tests: fasting glucose and lipids preferred; HbA1c if diabetes present/suspected: Not recorded / none performed.  
- Renal function and liver function tests if clinically indicated: Not recorded / none performed.  
- ECG if cardiac risk factors present or baseline: Not recorded.  
- Cervical screening if eligible and due: Not recorded.  
- Mammography if eligible and not up to date: Not recorded.  
- Faecal occult blood test if due: Not recorded.  
- Bone density (DEXA) if osteoporosis risk present: Not recorded.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key clinical findings and reasoning:
  - Acute severe unilateral (left-sided) headache woke patient from sleep (~05:30) and persisted through the morning. Mild photophobia and transient dizziness on waking. No fever, no neck stiffness, no nausea/vomiting, no focal neurological symptoms reported. Paracetamol taken with little benefit. History of anxiety and recent significant work-related stress / sleep disturbance.
  - Clinician impression in transcript: tension-type headache and migraine considered; first-line management recommended as ibuprofen and supportive measures; counselling and time off work advised; follow-up in one week.
  - DDx supports primary headache diagnoses (tension-type high likelihood; migraine and sleep-deprivation/dehydration medium likelihood) and flags urgent vascular causes (e.g., subarachnoid hemorrhage) as low-probability but important to consider if red flags develop.
- Working diagnosis: Tension-type headache (stress-related). Supported by: history of anxiety, prolonged work stress and late nights; clinician identified tension headache as a leading possibility; DDx ranks this as High likelihood.
- Considerations (additional plausible differentials from DDx consistent with transcript):
  - Migraine — Medium likelihood: unilateral pain and mild photophobia and typical triggers (stress, sleep disturbance) support this possibility.  
  - Headache secondary to sleep deprivation and/or dehydration — Medium likelihood: recent late nights and advice to increase fluids/sleep make this plausible.
  - Subarachnoid hemorrhage or intracranial vascular event — Low likelihood but considered: acute severe headache waking patient can represent SAH; transcript lacks red-flag features (no neck stiffness, vomiting, focal deficit); advise urgent reassessment if symptoms worsen or new neurological signs develop.
  - Medication-related headache (sertraline side effect, caffeine withdrawal) — Low likelihood per DDx; possible but no dose changes or caffeine history documented.
- Management plan documented in transcript:
  - Acute analgesia: start ibuprofen as first-line for suspected migraine/tension headache — ibuprofen dose/route/frequency not documented. Continue paracetamol if desired — dose/route/frequency not documented (patient already took paracetamol today).
  - Supportive measures: ensure 7–8 hours sleep per night; increase fluid intake to ~1.5–2 L/day (excluding coffee/tea); consider short period off work (clinician suggested ~1 week self-certified) to reduce stress.
  - Mental health support: clinician offered counselling service link for self-referral (patient advised to explore counselling).  
  - Safety netting: clinician provided information on headache danger signs and advised a low threshold to re-contact/return if symptoms worsen. If no improvement at follow-up, clinician may arrange blood tests or further investigations/imaging.
  - Follow-up: arranged in ~1 week with same service/another doctor as required.

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification: Advice given on improving sleep (7–8 hours/night), increasing hydration (1.5–2 L/day), and reducing work-related stress; counselling/self-referral suggested.  
- Patient health goals and priorities: Patient seeks relief of acute headache and reduction of work-related stress; agreed to follow recommended measures and to book follow-up.  
- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA): Not recorded.  
- Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports): Counselling service link provided for self-referral (documented). No other formal referrals recorded.  
- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled: Follow-up arranged in one week.

Consider

- Mental health support or counselling referral: Counselling self-referral offered and recommended (documented).  
- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management: Not recorded / not currently indicated.  
- Dental referral if oral health issues identified: Not recorded.  
- Optometry referral for visual concerns or regular screening: Not recorded; mild photophobia only.  
- Audiometry referral if hearing issues suspected: Not recorded.  
- Social work or housing support referral if social determinants affect health: Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Tension-type headache (High): History of anxiety, prolonged work stress and late nights; clinician and DDx rate this as most likely cause.  
- Migraine (Medium): Unilateral headache and mild photophobia with known triggers (stress, sleep disturbance) support this as a plausible alternative.  
- Headache secondary to sleep deprivation and/or dehydration (Medium): Recent late nights and potential inadequate hydration plausibly explain an acute morning headache; supported by clinician advice to improve sleep and fluids.

Quality checks
- Missing but clinically expected elements: No vital signs recorded (BP, HR), no neurological examination documented, no anthropometric data (height/weight/BMI), no immunisation status review, no baseline blood tests or ECG, no documentation of alcohol/substance use, and no formal headache severity scale / neuro exam recorded.  
- Internal conflicts or contradictions between transcript and DDx: None identified — DDx and transcript are concordant (transcript clinician and DDx both favor primary headache causes; DDx additionally lists lower-probability serious differentials).  
- Transcript quality notes: Dialogue complete and intelligible; no significant audio clarity issues noted.
